description: Pinned TypeScript corpus for measuring strata's real-world behaviour. Repositories are selected for size, activity, and measured AI-attributed commit share; each is pinned to an exact commit so a scan is reproducible and threshold changes are diffable.

aiAttribution.method: Of the 400 commits preceding the pinned commit, the share whose author or Co-authored-by trailer names a known coding agent.
aiAttribution.caveat: A lower bound on AI involvement, not a measurement of it. Only commits that DECLARE an agent are counted, and the declaration is per-commit, never per-file. No finding in this corpus should be described as AI-authored on the strength of this number.

repos.why: Highest measured agent share in the corpus, and the densest source of passThroughMethod candidates.
Highest measured agent share, and one of three targets that exercises all seven detectors. The gui target adds a .tsx-heavy arm.
Small, young, protocol-driven codebase — the shape a candidate scanner is most likely to be pointed at by a new adopter.
The corpus's densest source of passThroughExport candidates, and the only one where wideSignature and passThroughExport both rank high.
Largest single target in the corpus and the widest detector spread; carries the corpus's only meaningful wideSignature volume.
The one target where uniqueImplementation dominates — a provider-adapter codebase is exactly where speculative interfaces should either be justified or not.
Low-attribution contrast arm: mature, hand-written, heavily reviewed. Included so a per-KLOC number from the high-attribution repos has something to be read against.
Second contrast arm, and the target that first exposed the duplicateSymbol triviality families. Kept because a known-bad case belongs in a regression corpus.
